questions.q: 1 million series, 30 ms per series, 50 cores, ideal speed-up. How many minutes?
Which is a clear advantage of a global model?
options: It captures every unique quirk of each series perfectly
It can forecast series with short history by using similar series
why: Local models are better at unique quirks.
Correct: it learns shared patterns across series.
It usually needs id or group features.
Any model can overfit.

questions.q: Which are good scale practices? (pick all)
options: Score only series whose inputs changed
why: Whole series stay together on a worker.
Saves compute with a cache.
Overhead is larger than the work for small series.
A simple forecast beats a missing one.

questions.q: Scenario: 0.5% of series fail every night because of a bad value. What is the best handling?
options: Publish the rest, use the fallback for failed series, and alert with the count
why: One bad series would block millions.
Correct: partial success plus visibility.
Silent failure hides a real problem.
The business still needs a forecast for those items.

questions.q: Scenario: a team proposes a deep model that is 1% more accurate but 20 times slower than LightGBM, and the nightly window is already full. What do you say?
options: Accept; accuracy is the only goal
Reject or limit it to top-value series; the gain is small compared with the cost and risk
why: Cost and time limits are real requirements.
Correct: spend the extra compute only where value is high.
Weekly forecasts would be stale.
The window comes from the business.

options: The server is slow at 6 a.m.
A new series has little or no history to learn from
why: That is a startup delay, not cold start.
Correct.
That is a deployment problem.
Cold start is about new items, not seasons.
